extracted.intended_audience: government lawyers, Treasury/War Department accountants, and officials responsible for federal appropriations and military fund administration
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts rules for when and against which appropriation particular government expenses may properly be charged, with illustrations from Army/War Department practice and opinions. Covers interpretation principles, examples of allowable/incidental charges, and limits on use of appropriations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensive construction of remedial appropriation statutes
rubrics_metrics.description: Sections 19 and 20 of the river and harbor act of March 3, 1899 ... provide that 'whenever the navigation of any ... canals ... shall be obstructed or endangered by any sunken vessel, boat, water craft, raft, or other similar obstruction' the same may be removed by the Secretary of War. In view of the general purpose of the act, which was to keep the navigable waters clear of obstructions, the act should receive an extensive rather than a restrictive construction, and, therefore, the general words 'other similar obstructions' should not be closely restricted to obstructions of the nature of those specifically mentioned, but if in any way similar they should be regarded as coming within the purview of the act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an object (e.g., a draw span thrown into a canal and blocking navigation) is 'in any way similar' to listed obstructions and the object threatens navigation, it may be removed under the act; the appropriation tied to wreck removal is the proper appropriation to charge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Charge expenses to the specific appropriation for the purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: The act should be considered as making an appropriation for the specific purpose of removing wrecks, and therefore that act ... was the proper appropriation against which to charge the expense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a statute creates a specific-purpose appropriation, expenses for that specific purpose should be charged to it rather than to a more general, indefinite appropriation even if both could arguably apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imported government property: purchase price plus duties charged to same appropriation
rubrics_metrics.description: The appropriation that is chargeable with the purchase price of Government property imported into the Philippine Islands from the United States is also chargeable with the payment of customs duties and internal-revenue taxes legally assessed against the United States under the appropriation act of August 8, 1905 (36 Stat. 11 and 130).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Customs and internal revenue taxes legally assessed on imported government property are part of the cost and may be charged to the appropriation for the purchase.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary-purpose test for departmental chargeability
rubrics_metrics.description: If gas is needed not for heating or lighting, but for testing and sampling stores, the expenditure for the gas would not be one connected with the heating or lighting of the storehouse, but would be connected with the 'purchase, care,' etc., of subsistence supplies, and should, therefore, be a charge against the appropriation for the Subsistence Department.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine which appropriation to charge by asking the primary purpose of the expenditure (e.g., heating/lighting vs. testing subsistence).

rubrics_metrics.name: Medical/hospital equipment and operation charged to Medical appropriation
rubrics_metrics.description: As the expense connected with the installation and operation of electric fans for a military hospital is not an expense incident to lighting a military post, it should not be charged against the appropriation for the Quartermaster's Department, but against the appropriation for the 'Medical and Hospital Department.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expenses that are inherently medical/hospital in function (equipment or operation) belong to Medical appropriations rather than Quartermaster funds for lighting/housekeeping.

rubrics_metrics.name: Site-preparation removals charged to construction appropriation
rubrics_metrics.description: Where it was necessary to remove certain buildings under the control of the Ordnance Department to prepare a site for the erection of a hospital, the expense of the removal of the buildings should be charged against the appropriation for the construction of the hospital and the fact that the Ordnance Department had control of the buildings was not a material consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Control/ownership by another department does not bar charging site-preparation costs to the construction appropriation for the new work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Telephone message charges allocated by subject-matter
rubrics_metrics.description: Each message should be charged against that fund out of which the article to which the message referred was purchased. For instance, messages having to do exclusively with the sick ... should be paid out of hospital funds; but messages connected with the administration of the hospital, such as those relating to the purchase of medicines, hospital property, etc., should be paid for by the Quartermaster's Department.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allocate communication costs to the fund associated with the substantive subject of the message (patient care vs. administration/purchases).

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriations may cover incidental expenses necessary to achieve stated object
rubrics_metrics.description: The act appropriated for 'lighting and maintaining in good order each electric light ...' — held that the cost of necessary excavations and extension of underground conduits to carry the current for the new lights would be a proper charge against this appropriation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Necessary ancillary work (excavations, conduits) directly enabling an appropriated function may be charged to that appropriation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriation wording interpreted to include modern materials/means
rubrics_metrics.description: The appropriation for 'fuel and lights' ... may be deemed to contemplate gas as a material for lighting equally with the more primitive methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Older appropriation language can be interpreted to encompass modern equivalents (e.g., gas as lighting fuel) where that is consistent with the appropriation's purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experts' testing expenses chargeable to related operational appropriations
rubrics_metrics.description: The expense of obtaining the services of experts in connection with tests to determine economical use of coal at military posts would be a proper charge against the appropriations out of which the cost of fuel and heating apparatus is defrayed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Testing or expert fees that directly relate to economy/operation of an appropriated service can be charged to the operational appropriation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unexpended balances with no disposition language revert or divided pro rata
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the appropriation to become available when certain sums had been appropriated by others left a balance over and the act was completely lacking in words indicating what disposition should be made of this balance, held that the unexpended balance could not be turned over for care and maintenance; further, that the unexpended balance should be divided pro rata among those by whom the funds were provided and the portion belonging to the United States deposited to 'Miscellaneous receipts.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When appropriation language is silent, unexpended balances may be apportioned among original contributors rather than repurposed absent statutory authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriation 'for procuring water' can include purchase of distilled water
rubrics_metrics.description: A provision in an appropriation for ... 'procuring water and introducing the same to buildings ...' is sufficient to cover the purchase of distilled water at a division headquarters for the use of clerks where ordinary water procured ... is not fit for drinking purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpretations should allow necessary means to achieve the stated remedial objective (safe drinking water).

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriation for erecting public building generally excludes furniture
rubrics_metrics.description: No part of an appropriation which has been made for the erection of a public building can legally be used in the purchase of furniture therefor, except such in the nature of fixtures as may be considered a part of the building itself and necessary to complete it for the purposes stated in the appropriation act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Furniture is not payable from construction appropriations unless it qualifies as a fixture integral to the building's completion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transportation/construction appropriations cover reasonable repair of facilities used for military purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the head 'Army transportation,' money was expressly appropriated 'for constructing roads and wharves.' Held that the expense of repairing a crib dock and approach thereto belonging to the Government on the Fort Wayne Military Reservation, and used for military purposes, would be a proper charge against the said appropriation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Repair of government transportation infrastructure used for military purposes may be charged to transportation/construction appropriations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriations construed to include related utility infrastructure
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the Government required for military purposes a street in which were situated water mains and hydrants, held that the money appropriated for the purchase of the land could be expended for purchase of the mains and hydrants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acquisition appropriations may include necessary utility fixtures integral to the acquired property.

rubrics_metrics.name: Library appropriation may cover temporary labor hire for reclassification
rubrics_metrics.description: The appropriation 'for the library of the Surgeon General's office, including the purchase of necessary books of reference and periodicals' is broad enough to cover the hire of the laborers necessary in handling and carrying books in connection with the reclassification of the library.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Labor temporarily necessary to effectuate the statutory library purpose may be charged to the library appropriation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintenance/repair appropriations include travel expenses of employees engaged in repairs
rubrics_metrics.description: Appropriation for the 'maintenance and repair of military telegraph lines and cables, including salaries of civilian employees, supplies, and general repairs' was held sufficient to include the travel expenses of a civilian employee who was on temporary duty in Alaska as wireless inspector in connection with installation and overhauling apparatus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Travel reasonably incidental to maintenance/repair duties may be charged to the maintenance appropriation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriation permits professional services necessary to execute project
rubrics_metrics.description: The act for the marking, etc., of the graves ... covers 'proper fencing for the preservation of said burial grounds.' Held that the Secretary of War ... may employ an architect to design the fencing and attend to its construction and may pay him the usual compensation for such services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where means to accomplish an appropriated object are not specified, the officer may authorize necessary professional services and grading to carry out the appropriation's purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Materials taken from private land during authorized military exercises treated as purchased articles
rubrics_metrics.description: Where certain trees on private land were cut down for use in the construction of a pontoon bridge in the course of tactical instruction ... the trees should be considered as articles purchased for the use of the military establishment and the owner be paid the value out of the funds set apart for the use of the particular service school.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compensation for private property used in authorized exercises should be paid from the applicable service funds as if the articles had been purchased.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriations must expressly authorize uses not plainly included (negative example)
rubrics_metrics.description: The act ... provided for establishment of a military post ... including ... water supply, lighting, sewerage, and drainage ... Held that as the above statute did not specifically authorize the construction of 'roads,' it could not be used for such a purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an activity (e.g., road construction) is not reasonably necessary to the enumerated objects and is not specifically authorized, it cannot be charged to that appropriation.

rubrics_metrics.name: No appropriations for furnishing music to unauthorized volunteer bands
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no authority to expend public money in furnishing music to so-called 'volunteer bands,' as such bands are not authorized by law as a part of the military establishment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expenses for entities not legally authorized as part of the establishment are not chargeable to appropriations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Charges for prisoner confinement in state institutions not payable from Army appropriations when offense is local
rubrics_metrics.description: A native killed a United States soldier ... tried by military commission and sentenced ... confinement served in a state penitentiary. Held that the crime was one over which the courts of Porto Rico had jurisdiction ... therefore the bills connected with the keeping of this prisoner in a State penitentiary were not payable from any appropriation for the Army.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the criminal matter is within local civil jurisdiction, related imprisonment costs are not chargeable to military appropriations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriations for transport of remains limited by geographic scope language
rubrics_metrics.description: By act of July 8, 1898, $200,000 was appropriated 'to enable the Secretary of War ... to cause to be transported to their homes the remains of officers and soldiers who die at military camps or ... in the field at places 'outside of the limits of the United States.' Held that the appropriation could be used for providing metallic caskets and other expenses incident to disinterring the remains and preparing them for shipment ... But ... the act did not apply where the deceased ... died within the limits of the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chargeability is constrained by the statute's geographic limitations; incidental costs of authorized transportation (caskets, disinterment) are included when within scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disbursing officer authority to use total available balance not limited to same fiscal year
rubrics_metrics.description: Act of Congress ... authorizing a disbursing officer ... to make payment from the total available balance to his official credit provided sufficient funds ... apportioned by the Quartermaster General for the expenditure, was not limited to appropriations pertaining to the same fiscal year; there was nothing in the language of the appropriation which would justify such a limitation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory authority to make payments from available balances should be read by its language; absent explicit fiscal-year limitation, payments may cross fiscal years if apportionment permits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forfeiture of pay by civilian employee remains in original appropriation
rubrics_metrics.description: A civilian employee was sentenced by a court-martial to a forfeiture of pay. Held that the forfeiture should not be actually paid, but should remain in the appropriation from which the civilian was paid, the forfeiture being in effect a reduction of his authorized pay to that extent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Forfeited amounts reduce the payroll charge to the appropriation and remain within that appropriation rather than being separately paid out.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriation for maintaining cemetery may cover access-related construction
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the United States owned to the middle of a street adjoining a national cemetery, held that an appropriation 'for maintaining and improving national cemeteries' would cover the cost of construction of a sidewalk along the street if the sidewalk is considered as required for the convenience of access to the cemetery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an improvement on adjacent property is necessary for convenient access to an appropriated object, the cost may be charged to the cemetery-maintenance appropriation.
